options.title: Microsoft Bought Nokia's Phones. Two Years Later It Gave Up
options.first_line: Microsoft bought Nokia's phone business, the phone in every pocket, and two years later it gave up.
options.first_frame: An old Nokia brick phone on a table, its screen lit, as a stamp reading MICROSOFT lands across it.

options.title: Microsoft Paid Billions for Nokia. Then Wrote It Off
options.first_line: Microsoft paid billions of euros for Nokia's phones, then wrote almost all of it off.
options.first_frame: The 2013 Microsoft deal announcement as a typeset page, the price line highlighted in yellow, an old Nokia phone in the corner.

options.title: Nokia Was in Every Pocket. Microsoft Bought It Anyway
options.first_line: Nokia's phone was in every pocket, then Microsoft bought it, and two years later it was gone.
options.first_frame: A hand pulling an old Nokia phone out of a jeans pocket, the word NOKIA slamming in as a label.

why: It opens on a phone the viewer once had in their own pocket and its title holds back the ending, so you stay to learn why Microsoft bought it anyway and what happened, where A and B give away the give-up and the write-off in the title.
